statement: In a chess club, 60% of the members are girls. 20% of the girls and 45% of the boys play in tournaments. What percentage of the tournament players are girls?

choices.misconception: I gave the percentage of girls in the whole club.
I found the girls who play as a percentage of the whole club, not of the players.
I found what percentage of the whole club plays in tournaments.
I gave the percentage of girls who play, not the percentage of players who are girls.

hints: Percentages of different groups cannot be compared directly. Turn each one into a number of people out of 100 members, then compare the right two numbers.
Out of 100 members there are 60 girls, of whom 12 play, and 40 boys, of whom 18 play.

solutions.reliable: Suppose there are 100 members: 60 girls and 40 boys. Girls who play: 20% of 60 is 12. Boys who play: 45% of 40 is 18. So 30 members play, and 12 of them are girls: $\frac{12}{30} = \frac{2}{5} = 40\%$. The transferable idea: a percentage is always a percentage of something, so pick a convenient total and track what each percentage is taken of.

whyOnTest: Percentage questions test keeping track of what each percentage is taken of, especially when the whole changes from one step to the next.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
